newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU rejects calls to end tobacco subsidies.
newsitem.headline: EU rejects calls to end tobacco subsidies.

text.p: The European Commission proposed on Wednesday reforming the European Union's tobacco subsidy programme, but rejected calls for a complete end to the aid.
Despite criticism that the subsidies compromise the EU's efforts to curb smoking-related deaths, the Commission said it was not prepared to put 200,000 tobacco-related workers out of jobs.

"Given that approximately 77 percent of tobacco consumed in the EU is imported, the regime's abolition would merely lead to 100 percent of EU tobacco demand being met by imports," it said in a statement.

Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn, who waged an unsuccessful campaign to phase out the more than $1 billion a year in annual subsidies, told a news conference he was unhappy with the decision, calling smoking the biggest single preventable cause of death in the EU.
But he won support from the Commission for proposals EU governments should consider implementing to curb smoking and its damaging health effects.

These include strengthening cigarette label warnings, reducing the tar and nicotine content of cigarettes, regulating additives and agreeing a code of practice on children's right to a smoke-free environment.
The Commission has so far been unable to get EU ministers to agree an existing proposal to ban all tobacco advertising.
Flynn said the Commission would submit new legislative proposals only if it won support after consulting interested parties.

It proposed reforming the tobacco subsidy programme to target aid on higher-quality products, offer buyouts to entice farmers away from tobacco and double the one percent levy on subsidies that is used to finance an EU tobacco public health fund.

Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler said the Commission had no choice but to continue aiding farmers who had no way to diversify since their plantations were on average barely more than one hectare.
"We cannot offer any de facto alternatives to these families," he said.
Eight EU countries produce tobacco, but 76 percent of the production comes from Italy and Greece.
Flynn and Fischler said two commissioners had voted against the proposal and three had abstained, without naming names. Several of Flynn's colleagues supported his bid to end tobacco subsidies.
